speaker: narrator
text: If the world's internet went down tomorrow, what could your computer still do?

speaker: narrator
text: This open-source system was built for that day. It is called Project NOMAD.

speaker: narrator
text: The one catch is you download everything before you go offline. Full Wikipedia alone is about one hundred and twenty-five gigabytes.

speaker: narrator
text: All in one machine. You get medical references, offline survival guides, regional maps, and complete Khan Academy courses.

speaker: narrator
text: Plus local note-taking, data tools with CyberChef, and a supply depot app catalog running right on your device.

speaker: narrator
text: The basic system runs on almost anything. But running local AI wants a beefy PC, with thirty-two gigs of RAM and an RTX 3060.

speaker: narrator
text: It is completely free and open source with over forty-two thousand stars on GitHub. Check the pinned comment for all the links.
